launches.title: Particularity: AI investigators for government regulators
launches.tagline: AI agents that catch consumer protection violations before anyone complains
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We're Kavin and Chris.

**TL;DR:** Particularity gives federal, state, and city consumer protection agencies AI agents that check live websites for violations like junk fees, subscription traps, and deceptive ads and turn what they find into court-ready evidence.

<https://youtu.be/f6qVdEjYR9Y>

**What enforcement looks like today**

Chris and I found ourselves frustrated by the deluge of undisclosed advertising on social media (which violates FTC guidelines) and started thinking,“How does a government agency capture the true scope of illicit activity at scale?”

That question led us to find that most consumer protection regulation today still starts with a complaint. Investigators work through an inbox that never empties, while millions of websites change every day. Most people who are harmed never file at all. 

The result is ad hoc enforcement: few companies get caught and often years later. When breaking the rules rarely costs anything, competition stops being about who builds the better product and starts being about who's willing to cheat.

**What Particularity does**

\- **Uncover.** Agents check live websites the way a consumer would. Does the advertised price match checkout? Can you actually cancel online? Every step is captured, timestamped, and hashed.

\- **Investigate.** Every complaint gets a first-pass investigation within the same minute, matched against evidence already on file.

\- **Act.** Findings map to the elements of the law, so staff can move straight to a warning letter or enforcement action.

**About us**

Kavin worked at a causal inference startup and on consumer protection and capital markets at the Senate Banking Committee. Chris built security and compliance infrastructure at AWS, including services for the EU Sovereign Cloud. \
\
**If you’re a regulator, please reach out!**

We’re interested in talking to consumer protection staff at state AG offices, large city consumer affairs departments, and state agencies. We’d also love to talk to any former FTC or CFPB folks and others generally in the consumer protection space.
